evidence_quotes.quote: The article aims to provide a historical overview of the factors that induced or influenced early water and water and sanitation public policy in Brazil.
Usa-se a perspectiva histórica para rastrear alguns desenvolvimentos em recursos hídricos e saneamento no período que vai do desembarque português até a década de 1930.

Adotou-se uma perspectiva analítica que enfatiza a dependência de estruturas econômicas, sociais e políticas de países periféricos em relação a um sistema mundial hierarquizado e desigual, ao qual se articulam de modo subordinado (CEPAL, 2014).
A pesquisa documental foi conduzida especialmente nos arquivos da Biblioteca Nacional e em sítios eletrônicos governamentais, especializados em legislação e com registros administrativos.
Trata-se do processo de mercadorização da água por meio do serviço de abastecimento público, da apropriação e comercialização de um bem até então tratado como bem de acesso irrestrito.

A prerrogativa de regular tarifas públicas, especialmente da energia elétrica, como meio de controlar importante fator de produção industrial, estabelecer-se-ia com a decretação do Código de Águas em 1934, o primeiro grande marco legislativo da gestão das águas no país, estabelecido em um contexto de centralização administrativa, fortalecimento do poder central e nacionalismo.

criterion_notes.c1: Touches on urban water supply and sewerage service provision in historical perspective (colonial public fountains/chafarizes, 19th-century piped water and sewerage networks, and socio-spatial exclusion of poorer urban populations), alongside broader water-resources management for mining and hydroelectricity.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, this paper passes because it examines historical public policies, regulatory frameworks, private utility concessions (e.g., Decree 1.929 of 1857), urban hygienist regulations, and the 1934 Water Code (Código de Águas). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading, however, it fails: the paper is a macro-governance political-economy overview (using CEPAL historical-structural / world-systems theory from the colonial era to the 1930s) rather than an analysis of a specific rule-type mechanism directly governing household service access, even though it briefly notes in narrative terms that 19th-century private concessionaires targeted areas with ability to pay and municipalities demolished free public fountains. (Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall study decision remains exclude due to lack of empirical evidence under Criterion 3.)
criterion_notes.c3: Fails Criterion 3 (exclude as E05): This is a narrative historical essay / macro-policy overview spanning from the Portuguese colonial arrival to the 1930s. Although it states that documentary consultation was conducted in the National Library and government legislation websites, the text synthesizes classic Brazilian social/economic historiography (Furtado, Prado Jr., Ribeiro) and secondary sanitation histories (e.g., Rezende & Heller, Meade, Graham, Rolnik, Braadbaart) plus legislative/doctrinal texts (Decree 1.929 of 1857; Valladão 1907 on the Water Code). It presents no primary empirical data on service access, no qualitative or quantitative empirical investigation of households/communities/utilities, and is not a systematic empirical synthesis.
criterion_notes.c4: Does not report any empirical outcome data on water or sanitation access, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, or affordability; contains only broad secondary narrative statements about historical exclusion of low-income groups.
criterion_notes.c5: As a macro-historical narrative essay covering four centuries of national history without an empirical sample or unit of analysis, it does not provide an identifiable empirical population, exposure, and outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with abstracts in Portuguese, English, and Spanish), which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Narrative historical policy overview / historical-structural essay (non-empirical)
exposure: Macro-historical political-economic and public policy trajectory in sanitation and water resources in Brazil (colonial period to 1934 Water Code), including 19th-century private utility concessions and hygienist urban reforms
rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence). The paper is a narrative macro-historical essay / policy overview applying CEPAL historical-structural and world-systems perspectives to trace the formation of sanitation and water-resources policies in Brazil from the colonial era to the 1934 Water Code. It relies on classic Brazilian economic/social historiography, secondary sectoral histories, and statutory/doctrinal texts (e.g., Decree 1.929 of 1857 and Valladão 1907) without collecting or analysing primary empirical data on household or community water/sanitation service access, and it is not a systematic empirical synthesis. In addition, under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, its primary analytical focus is macro-governance background and water-resources regulation for hydroelectricity rather than a rule-type mechanism governing household access; even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, it remains excluded for lack of empirical access evidence (E05).
